message.content:
### The “Best” Sushi in Los Angeles – A Quick Guide

Los Angeles is a sushi mecca, and picking the single “best” spot is a matter of taste, budget, and what you’re after (traditional Edomae, creative rolls, or a high‑end omakase). Below is a curated list of the most celebrated sushi restaurants in LA, ranked by overall reputation, quality, and experience. Feel free to pick the one that matches your vibe!

| Rank | Restaurant | Location | What Makes It Stand Out | Price Range | Notes |
|------|------------|----------|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| **1** | **Sushi Ota** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Legendary Edomae sushi, meticulous fish selection, simple yet perfect nigiri. | $30–$70 per person | Closed on Mondays; reservations essential. |
| **2** | **Sushi Gen** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Classic Edomae, renowned for its toro and sashimi. | $35–$80 per person | Also closed on Mondays; highly sought after. |
| **3** | **Sushi Park** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | A blend of traditional and modern, known for its omakase and creative rolls. | $40–$90 per person | Great for both sushi purists and adventurous diners. |
| **4** | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Intimate setting, chef‑driven omakase, emphasis on seasonal fish. | $50–$100 per person | Reservations required; no take‑out. |
| **5** | **Sushi Kappo** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Contemporary kaiseki‑style sushi, excellent for special occasions. | $60–$120 per person | Ideal for a refined dining experience. |
| **6** | **Sushi Neko** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Trendy spot with a playful menu, great for casual sushi lovers. | $20–$50 per person | Good for a relaxed night out. |
| **7** | **Sushi Saito** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | High‑end omakase, Michelin‑star quality, limited seating. | $80–$150 per person | Very exclusive; book months in advance. |
| **8** | **Sushi Tatsu** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Known for its fresh fish and creative rolls, friendly staff. | $25–$55 per person | Great for a casual sushi fix. |
| **9** | **Sushi Katsu** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Classic Japanese sushi with a modern twist, excellent for groups. | $30–$60 per person | Good for larger parties. |
| **10** | **Sushi Maki** | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, West Hollywood | Affordable, quick service, solid quality sushi. | $15–$35 per person | Ideal for a quick bite. |

> **Tip:** All of the top‑tier spots (Sushi Ota, Sushi Gen, Sushi Park, etc.) share the same address—1120 S. La Brea Ave in West Hollywood. They’re part of the same family of restaurants, each offering a slightly different style of sushi. Reservations are a must, especially for the omakase experiences.

---

#### How to Choose

| Preference | Best Match |
|------------|------------|
| **Traditional Edomae** | Sushi Ota, Sushi Gen |
| **Creative Rolls & Modern Twist** | Sushi Park, Sushi Neko |
| **High‑End Omakase** | Sushi Tetsu, Sushi Kappo, Sushi Saito |
| **Casual & Affordable** | Sushi Maki, Sushi Tatsu |
| **Special Occasion** | Sushi Kappo, Sushi Saito |

---

#### Quick Booking Tips

1. **Reserve Early** – Especially for the top‑tier spots; they often book months in advance.
2. **Check Closing Days** – Many of the premium places close on Mondays.
3. **Omakase vs. À la Carte** – Omakase is a set menu; à la carte lets you pick individual pieces.
4. **Dress Code** – Most places are casual, but some high‑end spots appreciate a smart‑casual look.

Enjoy your sushi adventure in LA! If you need more details (menu highlights, chef bios, or how to get there), just let me know.
